title: Possible short alphanumeric password in a URL in source
description: A short alphanumeric password in a URL sits in a URL's userinfo in plain text. URL userinfo syntax declares the part after the colon to be a password, so an 8-11 character alphanumeric value there is credential-shaped: anyone who can read the repository can use it until it is rotated. Shape-only: the match cannot prove the value is live, and short alphanumeric strings are weak evidence on their own (mandatory LOW confidence).
remediation: Treat the URL as containing a credential: rotate the value, review access logs of the service it names for use of the old value, and load credentials from a secret manager or environment at run time instead of committing them in URLs.
limitation: Shape-only heuristic over URL userinfo syntax. 8-11 alphanumeric characters with mixed case and a digit, placeholder-vetoed. Pure lowercase words, pure numbers, symbols (see the symbol variant), and values shorter than 8 or longer than 11 alphanumeric characters are out of scope. Cannot prove the value is live.
